function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• Rural interstate: 70 mph (except 55 mph on I‑35).
• Urban interstate: 65 mph.
• Residential streets: 25–35 mph (often 25 mph).
• School zones: 20 mph during school hours. | Texas Transportation Code §§ 545.001‑545.004 | | **Seat‑Belt & Child Restraint** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 years or 4 ft 9 in tall must use a child restraint system.
• Rear‑seat child restraints are mandatory until age 13 or 4 ft 9 in. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.005 | | **DUI / Alcohol** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal for drivers over 21.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02 %).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code §§ 545.021‑545.023 | | **Texting & Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited (unless hands‑free).
• Texting while driving is illegal. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.025 | | **Headlights & Signals** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather.
• Turn signals must be used at least 100 ft before turning. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.030 | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.
• Stop at stop signs and red lights.
• Give right‑of‑way to emergency vehicles with flashing lights. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.040 | | **Parking** | • No parking within 20 ft of a fire hydrant.
• No parking in front of a driveway or on a sidewalk.
• Parking in a handicap space requires a valid permit. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.050 | | **School Bus** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• No passing a stopped school bus with flashing red lights. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.060 | | **Lane Discipline** | • Keep to the right lane unless passing.
• Do not drive in the left lane on a two‑lane road unless passing. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.070 | | **Vehicle Registration & Insurance** | • Must display valid registration and proof of insurance.
• Failure to register or insure can lead to fines and vehicle impoundment. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.080 | | **Special Rules** | • “No‑stop” zones on I‑35 (no stopping or parking).
• “No‑passing” zones on I‑35 (no passing). | Texas Transportation Code §§ 545.090‑545.095 | ### How to Stay Updated 1. **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** – Official website: [https://www.txdot.gov](https://www.txdot.gov) 2. **Texas Transportation Code** – Accessible online via the Texas Legislature’s website. 3. **Local County Courts** – For specific local ordinances or recent changes. 4. **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)** – For registration, licensing, and insurance requirements. ### Quick Tips - **Always check posted signs** – Speed limits and special rules can vary by county or city. - **Use hands‑free devices** – If you need to talk or listen to music, keep your hands on the wheel. - **Keep your vehicle in good condition** – Proper lighting, brakes, and tires are essential for safety and compliance. - **Carry required documents** – Driver’s license, registration, and proof of insurance should be in the vehicle at all times. Feel free to let me know if you’d like more detailed information on a specific area (e.g., DUI penalties, school bus rules, or local ordinances).
